paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus can handle your hard questions. John the Baptist was sitting in prison when he sent his disciples to ask, "Are You the One who was to come, or should we look for someone else?" (Matthew 11:3). Jesus didn't scold him. He pointed to what was happening: "The blind receive sight, the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the good news is preached to the poor" (Matthew 11:5). Bring Him the question, baker, and let Him answer with the evidence.

Then Jesus says, "Blessed is the one who does not fall away on account of Me" (Matthew 11:6). I think that blessing is for anybody whose life didn't go the way they pictured. You can be stuck in a hard place and still hold on to Him, because He is who He says He is. Jesus also lifted up John in front of the crowds. He called him "more than a prophet" (Matthew 11:9) and said that he is the messenger who prepared the way (Matthew 11:10). Waiting in a cell didn't make John small to Jesus, and your waiting won't make you small either.

The last part is a warning, and I'm taking it to heart. Jesus says that John came neither eating nor drinking, and they said, "He has a demon!" Then the Son of Man came eating and drinking, and they said, "Look at this glutton and drunkard" (Matthew 11:18-19). When people don't want to believe, no messenger will ever be the right one. Jesus ends with, "But wisdom is vindicated by her actions" (Matthew 11:19). So look at what He does, baker, and let that settle who He is.
